title: Hand off, reject, and release from the TUI
lead: The TUI can start, park, and mark done. It cannot hand a slice to review, send a review back, or clear a claim. Those operations already exist on the CLI.
findings_note: user request: handoff is CLI-only, so the TUI cannot finish or return a review
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the `v` view cycle (s165); changing handoff, reject, or release rules; a claim column.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A reviewer who lives in the TUI has no key for the review loop. The keys have to call the existing operations for the selected item only. The shortcut strip is two rows at 80 columns and one row at 160. s165 adds `v view`. Three new strip hints would wrap a third row. Help can carry the less common keys.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `h` hands off the selected item. An empty note prompt still hands off. A cancel writes nothing.
2. `x` rejects the selected item and requires a note. An empty note cancels and writes nothing.
3. `l` clears the claim and leaves the status unchanged.
4. Each action uses the existing op on the selected item only.
5. `?` lists `h`, `x`, and `l`. The visible strip gains `h handoff` and not the other two. With `v view` also present, the strip is still two rows at 80 columns and one row at 160.
6. `J` and `K` stay disabled while a filter or a view preset is active.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Bind `h` to handoff with an optional note, `x` to reject with a required note, and `l` to release. Put `h handoff` on the shortcut strip and the other two in help. Keep the strip inside the row budget above even when the s165 view hint is present.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer check`, and `git diff --check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, including the re-rendered roadmap and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.
